message_fragments.text: ...anyone on this channel... the blast door closed on me... sub-level two... the cold room... I have hours, not days...
message_fragments.outcome_hint: He states his remaining hours like a shift report.

message_fragments.text: ...this is Pavel, shift supervisor, Meridian Cold Store... the door sequencer failed during the storm... I have a lamp and a coat... the stock is still frozen, but I am too...
message_fragments.outcome_hint: He reports the failure, then the inventory, then himself.

message_fragments.text: ...day two. The lamp died. I can hear the compressors still running, which means the grid is up, which means someone is up... if you can hear this, the manual release is on the wall by the west rack, but I cannot reach it, the frost has... I cannot feel my fingers...
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The compressors still run — the grid is up somewhere.

message_fragments.text: ...day three. I am writing this down in case the recorder keeps it. The stock here is seed potatoes, not meat, the manifest was wrong, or I read it wrong in the dark. There are forty crates. If the door opens, they are for the spring planting, the co-op was counting on them. Do not eat them. Pavel out.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: Forty crates of seed potatoes — the co-op was counting on them.

message_fragments.text: ...this is the last broadcast from sub-level two. The compressors stopped an hour ago. I am leaving the recorder running. Take the potatoes. Find my daughter, her name is Rima, she was at the grange when the storm came. Tell her the door was not her fault. I told her to go ahead of me. Meridian Cold Store, out.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: He records for whoever opens the door next.

message_fragments.text: ...mayday, mayday, this is the barge Olenka, we are adrift, the tow snapped... position is... the river is taking us west... we have fuel but no steerage...
message_fragments.outcome_hint: Position, drift, and fuel — a crew used to paperwork.

message_fragments.text: ...Olenka, day two. The current has us. We passed the red buoy this morning, the one with the bell. If you know the river you know that means we are past the last bridge. There are three of us. The dog is fine. We have fuel for the lamp but the water is the problem...
message_fragments.outcome_hint: A bell buoy sounds behind the mayday — they are drifting.

message_fragments.text: ...day three. We hit something in the night. The hull is sound but the rudder is gone, we are spinning now, slowly, the river is wide here. I can see a light on the south bank, it is steady, it might be a house. If it is a house and you hear this, we are the barge with the single lamp, please...
message_fragments.outcome_hint: A steady light on the south bank — a house, or the hope of one.

message_fragments.text: ...this is Olenka, final. We have made the south bank. The light was a house, it was empty, it has a stove. We are beached on a sandbar and we can walk at dawn. The fuel stays on the barge, it is too heavy to move, mark it for whoever comes next. Three of us, and the dog. Olenka, out and grateful.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The rudder is gone; the hull holds.

message_fragments.text: ...is this on... we are on the roof, the school, Primary 14, the water came up fast... there are children here, eleven of them, I am the only adult... please...

...day two. The water is at the second floor. We have the roof hatch and we have the tarp from the gym. The children are being brave. The youngest, Dima, he is six, he has not cried. I do not know if that is good. We have the lunch crates, they were delivered yesterday, we have food for... I am counting...

...day three. A boat went past this morning, it did not see us, or it pretended not to. I waved the tarp. The children waved. The boat kept the middle of the street. We have enough food for four more days if I am careful. I am being careful. Dima spoke today, he asked if the water is going home. I said yes.

...day four. The water is going down, slowly, you can see the windows on the ground floor now, they are still under but you can see them. We moved the crates to the high side. One of the older children, Anya, she is twelve, she has been keeping the roll, she is better at it than me, she is a teacher already...

...day five. The water is below the first floor. We can see the yard. There is a boat there, the same boat, it is moored now, someone has been here. We are going down tomorrow, all of us, the hatch is the only way and I will go first. If anyone hears this and comes, we are eleven children and one teacher and we are coming down at dawn...

...day six, morning. We are down. The boat was ours, the one from day three, they came back in the night, they left water and a note. We are going with them. The school is intact, the lunch crates are intact, the roll is intact. Eleven children, one teacher, all present. Primary 14, out. Dima waved at the water.

radio_broadcasts.source_name: Salt Mine Survey Team — Emergency Beacon

message_fragments.text: ...this is surveyor three, I took a wrong turn off the main drift, the marker lights are down... I have a lamp and a radio and a little water... the rock is stable... I am not panicking...
message_fragments.outcome_hint: He reports the rock's stability before his own water.

message_fragments.text: ...day two. I found the survey station, the one from the seventies, the one they sealed. It is not sealed. Someone has been here, recently, there are footprints in the dust and they are not mine. There is a cache: water, candles, a notebook. The notebook is in a language I do not read but the diagrams are the mine diagrams, someone has been mapping...
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The survey station was sealed for a reason.

message_fragments.text: ...day three. I followed the footprints. They go deeper, not out. I do not understand. The notebook has dates, recent dates, someone was here two weeks ago. There is a second cache further in, larger, with a cot and a lamp that still has oil. Someone lives here, or lived here. I am going to leave a note and turn back...
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The footprints go deeper, not out.

message_fragments.text: ...day four. I am out. I found the main drift by following my own footprints back, which is how I should have done it the first time. The sealed station is on the map, it was never sealed, the map was wrong. I am leaving the notebook where I found it. If the person who lives down here hears this: I did not take your maps. Surveyor three, out.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: He followed his own prints back — the only way out.

message_fragments.text: ...this is Kestrel-9, the relay on the ridge, I am the operator, I stayed when the others went down... the wind took the road... the repeater is up, that is why you hear me... I have power for a week if I am careful...

...day two. The road is gone, not blocked, gone, the whole south face came down in the rain. I can see the valley from here. There are lights, three of them, in the valley, they are not moving. I do not know if they are people or houses. I am broadcasting because the repeater is the only one still up in this sector...

...day three. The three lights are people, I saw a fire this morning, they are people. I cannot reach them, the road is gone and the slope is loose. I am relaying their traffic too, I heard a woman call for a doctor this morning, I do not have a doctor, I have a relay, I passed it on, that is what I can do...

...day four. The wind has been steady for two days, the antenna is humming, it is the only music up here. I have been reading the logbook from the last operator, he left in the spring, he wrote that the ridge is a good place to watch the end of things from, he was not wrong, but he was not right either, the end is slow...

...day five. The valley people are gone, the fire is out, I hope they moved, I do not know. I am still up. The repeater is still up. I will keep it up as long as the power holds, that is the job, the job is the thing that keeps the shape of the day...

...day six. Power is low. I am broadcasting less. If you hear this and you have power, the repeater takes over on its own when I stop, it will relay whatever it hears, it does not need me, I was only here to watch it...

...day seven. This is the last operator log from Kestrel-9. The power is going. The repeater will stay up on its reserve. I am leaving the logbook open on the desk, and the coffee tin is half full, it is for the next operator, there is always a next operator. Relay station Kestrel-9, operator out. The wind is still humming.

...greybell caravan, we are held in the pass, the snow came in behind us... we have the mules and we have the trade but we cannot move forward or back... we are seven, plus the muleteer's boy... we have feed for three days...
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The mules' feed is counted before the people's food.

message_fragments.text: ...day two. We dug the lead mule out by morning. The boy is keeping the animals calm, he has a way with them, he is maybe ten. We have moved the trade goods to the high cart, the one with the canvas, if we lose a cart we lose the low one, that was the decision, the muleteer agreed...
message_fragments.outcome_hint: Mules stamp behind the report — a real caravan.

message_fragments.text: ...day three. The pass is clearing, we can see the far valley, it is green, which means it is lower, which means it is warmer. We are going to try to move at dawn. The trade is salt and iron, it is heavy, but the mules are rested, they have eaten, we have eaten, the boy found a way to make the hard bread soft, he is useful, that boy...
message_fragments.outcome_hint: Salt and iron — a caravan that trades, not begs.

message_fragments.text: ...day four. We are moving. The pass is open enough. We lost the low cart, the snow took it in the night, but the trade is on the high cart, the salt and the iron, we are walking with the mules. The boy is on the lead mule, he is singing, I do not know the song, the muleteer does, it is his...
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The pass is clearing from the far side.

message_fragments.text: ...day five. We are down. The far valley is a town, it is occupied, they have a market. We are trading the salt, the iron we are keeping, the muleteer says iron is for friends not strangers. The boy is eating a fruit, an actual fruit, he has never seen one, he is holding it like it is a lamp. Greybell caravan, out, and trading.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: They traded the low cart for passage.

message_fragments.text: ...this is the basement, District Hospital 3, the generator is the only power in the building... I am the night nurse, I stayed... there are four patients who cannot be moved, two on the ward, two in the cold room... the fuel is low...

...day two. I have moved the two from the ward to the basement, it is warmer here, the generator gives heat. The two in the cold room I cannot move, they are the ones who... I am keeping the generator for the cold room, the cold room is the reason, the generator is for them...

...day three. The fuel is the question. I have been rationing it, an hour on, two hours off. The cold room holds the cold for the off hours, it is designed to. The two from the ward are stable, they are sleeping, they do not know the power is going, I have not told them, there is no need...

...day four. A man came, he was looking for medicine, he was not a doctor. I gave him what I could spare, which was not much. He offered fuel, from a car, he said there is a car at the bottom of the hill. I cannot leave to get it. He said he would bring it. He left. I do not know if he will come back...

...day five. He came back. With the fuel. He would not give his name. He would not stay. He said the car was his sister's, and she did not need it now, and he left. The fuel is in the generator. The cold room is cold. The two from the ward are awake and they ate, I found food in the canteen, it is not much but it is food...

...day six. The fuel is enough for two more days. The two in the cold room are... the cold room is doing what it does. The man came back once more, in the night, he left more fuel and a note that said 'for the nurse who stayed.' I do not know him. I will keep the generator as long as there is fuel, and then I will keep the patients as long as there is me. District Hospital 3, basement, out.

...this is Cape Verity, the light is automated, I am the keeper, I stayed because the light is not the only thing that needs keeping... the boat did not come... the sea is up... I have the lamp and the clock...

...day two. The sea is down. The boat did not come. The light is on, it is automatic, it does not need me, but I am here. There is a ship, far out, it is not moving, it is riding the swell, it has no lights, I do not know if it is crewed. I am flashing the light at it, the light is for the rocks, but I am flashing it at the ship...

...day three. The ship is gone, or it was never there, the fog was thick and the fog makes shapes. The clock is still keeping time, the clock is the only thing that is. I have food for a week, the keeper before me left a store, he was organized, he left a list, the list is on the wall, I am following the list...

...day four. A boat, a small boat, it came close, I called to it, it did not answer, it may not have had a radio. It went south, toward the village, I hope it makes it, the sea is kind today. I am leaving the light on, the light is the point of the place, the point is not me...

...day five. The boat came back, with people, three, they are in the village, they are well, they saw the light, they said the light was the reason they came in. I did not tell them the light is automatic. I let them think I kept it. The keeper before me kept it, and the keeper after me will keep it, and the light keeps itself, and that is the truth, and the truth is not what they needed. Cape Verity, out.

...this is North Dam, the spillway is stuck, the gate will not close, the river is up, the reservoir is rising... I have the manual winch but it takes two, I am one... if the water overtops the emergency spill it is the town downstream...

...day two. I have been on the winch for sixteen hours, the gate moves, it moves, it is not enough. The water is at the second mark. I sent the family downstream, my wife and the girl, they went at dawn, I told them to go to the high school and not to come back until I call. I have not called...

...day three. The gate closed. It closed at four in the morning, I do not remember the last hour, I was on the winch and then the gate was closed and I was on the floor. The reservoir is dropping. The town is fine, I do not know if they know. I am going to leave the winch locked and walk down at dawn, I am going to the high school...

...day four. I am down. The high school is full, the town is fine, they did not know, the water never came. My wife is there, the girl is there, she is asleep, she does not know about the dam, I will not tell her yet. The gate is closed, the winch is locked, the dam is the dam. North Dam, out, and going home.
...seven, fourteen, three, nine, twenty-two, seven, fourteen, three, nine, twenty-two... [the loop is steady, unhurried, a woman's voice, reading numbers in a language no one speaks here]...
message_fragments.outcome_hint: Five numbers, one voice, no station identification.

message_fragments.text: ...seven, fourteen, three, nine, twenty-two... [the loop continues, but at 03:14 it stops, and the voice says, clearly, in the local tongue: 'the water is at the second step.' Then the loop resumes.]...
message_fragments.outcome_hint: At 03:14 the loop breaks — every night, the same minute.

message_fragments.text: ...seven, fourteen, three, nine, twenty-two... [the loop continues. At 03:14 the voice says: 'the water is at the third step. The gate is open.' The loop resumes. The river is at the third step. The gate is the dam. The dam operator has not called.]...
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The inserted line reads water levels like a gauge.

message_fragments.text: ...seven, fourteen, three, nine, twenty-two... [the loop continues. At 03:14 the voice says: 'the water is at the fourth step. The gate is closed. The man is on the floor.' The loop resumes. The dam operator called this morning. He said the gate closed at four. He said he was on the floor.]...
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The inserted voice knows the loop's schedule.

message_fragments.text: ...seven, fourteen, three, nine, twenty-two... [the loop continues. At 03:14 the voice says: 'the man is down. The girl is asleep. The water is going home.' The loop resumes. The dam operator is down. The girl is asleep. The water is going home. The voice knows what it should not. The loop does not care that you know.]...
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The voice is counting something besides the numbers.

message_fragments.text: ...echo-4, we lost the map in the river, the case opened... we are four, we know the general direction but not the route... we have rations for three days... we are not lost, we are mapless, there is a difference...
message_fragments.outcome_hint: He corrects himself before anyone else can.

message_fragments.text: ...day two. We found a road, it is not on any list, it is paved, it goes east, we are following it. There are houses, empty, one had a meal on the table, cold, we did not take it, we took the water. The sergeant says the road will meet the highway, the highway goes home...
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The paved road is on no survey list.

message_fragments.text: ...day three. The road does not meet the highway, it meets a river, the same river that took the map. There is a bridge, it is intact, we are crossing. On the far side there is a sign, it is for a town we do not know, the sign is new, the town is not on any old map, we are going to the town...
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The sign on the far bank is new — the town is not on any old map.

message_fragments.text: ...day four. The town is real, it is occupied, they have a radio, they let us use it, this is it. They are not on our maps because they are not from our maps, they are from before, they say. They are kind. They fed us. The sergeant is crying, he has not cried, he is crying now, we are safe, that is why...
message_fragments.outcome_hint: A town with a working radio answered them.

message_fragments.text: ...day five. We are staying. The sergeant says we are staying. The town does not need our maps and we do not need our maps here. They have a school and a well and a woman who keeps the radio. We are four, and now we are four more. Echo-4, out, and home, a different home, but home.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The sergeant decided to stay — the maps stayed too.

message_fragments.text: ...this is allotment seven, the greenhouse, the glass is mostly gone and the heater is out... I have one seedling, it is the winter wheat, the one we were saving... I have a lamp and a little paraffin... I am keeping the frost off it with the lamp and a jar...
message_fragments.outcome_hint: One seedling and a jar — a garden, not a settlement.

message_fragments.text: ...day two. The seedling is up, it is pale, it is the only green thing in the allotment. The frost took the rest in the first night. I have moved it to the bench under the remaining pane, the pane is cracked but it holds the heat of the lamp. The paraffin is the question, I have three nights...
message_fragments.outcome_hint: One seedling, one heater, one voice — an allotment, not a settlement.

message_fragments.text: ...day three. I went to the shed for the paraffin, there was a can, half full, someone left it, or forgot it, I am taking it as a loan, I will repay it in wheat, if the wheat lives. The seedling has a second leaf, it is small and it is green and it is the only green thing I have seen in a week...
message_fragments.outcome_hint: He calls a found can of paraffin a loan.

message_fragments.text: ...day four. A child came, from the next allotment, she is maybe eight, she came to see if anyone was here. She saw the seedling. She asked if she could name it. I said yes. She named it Tuesday, because that is the day. She is coming back on Tuesday. I do not know if she knows the wheat is for eating, not for naming...
message_fragments.outcome_hint: Someone left paraffin in the shed.

message_fragments.text: ...day five. Tuesday came, the child came, she brought a candle, she said the candle was for Tuesday, the wheat, to keep it warm. I lit the candle by the seedling. The child is right, the candle is for Tuesday. The paraffin is low, the candle is low, the wheat is up, it is the only thing that is up...

...day six. The wheat is in the ground, I moved it to the cold frame, it is hardy, it is winter wheat, it is meant for this. The child came with her mother, the mother saw the wheat and she sat down, she did not speak, she sat and she looked, and then she said 'we will share the bread.' I said yes. Allotment seven, out, and planting.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The child visits on Tuesdays.

message_fragments.text: ...almshouse... eight beds... asking for supplies, not rescue... wait...
message_fragments.outcome_hint: Supplies, not rescue — the caller corrects the band's purpose.

message_fragments.text: This is the almshouse clinic. We are full of a fever I can name but not stop. I am not asking to leave. I am asking for hands.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The clinic states odds, not pleas.

message_fragments.text: If anyone is counting: sixteen bedrolls, two doctors if the first one sleeps, and one door that stays open at the appointed hour. That is the inventory.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The inventory is exact to the bedroll.

message_fragments.text: Odds stated. Work continues. Come for the people, or come for me, or do not come. The kettle will be on either way.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The kettle will be on either way.

message_fragments.text: ...maintenance band... grounds are on... this is not an emergency, this is a census...
message_fragments.outcome_hint: This is a census, not a distress call.

message_fragments.text: One engineer at substation omega, badges expired, grounds checked daily. The grid is fine. The grid has no customers. Requesting copper before winter makes the survey lie to us.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: Badges expired — he counts himself as staff.

message_fragments.text: Parts list follows at the same hour tomorrow. Do not send hands I have to teach from zero; send hands who will respect a switching order, or send the parts alone.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The parts list is scheduled, not requested.

message_fragments.text: Repeat at the stated hour tomorrow. The grounds are on. The grounds stay on.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The engineer wants trained hands, not rescuers.

message_fragments.text: Final maintenance band. The survey crew has not arrived. I am leaving the switching order and the copper request at the east gate; if the grid wakes, it will be because someone chose to read it first.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The survey crew never came.

message_fragments.text: ...checking... this frequency is not monitored... objection follows, dated, signed...
message_fragments.outcome_hint: He calls his objection an objection — and puts it in writing.

message_fragments.text: To anyone holding: I wrote my objections in the margins and the margins ran out. I am where the sweeps do not look first. I am not asking to be turned in and I am not asking to be armed. Provisions are the lawful thing I am asking for.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The objections are dated and signed — a record, not a plea.

message_fragments.text: If the garrison answers first, the kit goes to whoever finds it and I go quiet. If the shelter answers first — thank you, and I am sorry, and the field kit is already yours in trust.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: Whoever answers first inherits the kit.

message_fragments.text: Automated watch, relay mast. Logged contact attempts unanswered for six days. Somebody may still be counting the stations that answer.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: Six days of unanswered contact attempts, all logged.

message_fragments.text: Correction, manual key: the watch is mine, the silence is not automated. A survey party is mapping towers in this region and mine is on their schedule, not mine.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: Contact attempts logged unanswered for six days.

message_fragments.text: The log is copied in two hands, one to send, one to lose. If the station goes dark on schedule it was planned. If it goes dark off schedule — ask the survey party.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The watch is manual — a person is up there.

message_fragments.text: Next transmission at the stated hour, whether or not anyone is counting. Signing on schedule.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The log is copied in two hands.

message_fragments.text: ...motel... he keeps the volume low... room fourteen... I can hear the vacancy sign buzzing...
message_fragments.outcome_hint: A vacancy sign buzzes behind the whisper.

message_fragments.text: This is room fourteen at the Verity Motel. There are two of us: me, and the man holding the door shut. He wants the fuel in the ice machine room. I want to be a person, not a payment.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: A vacancy sign buzzes behind the whisper.

message_fragments.text: He lets me key the set at noon to show I am still worth feeding. If nobody answers by the fourth day, he says the offer expires. I do not think he means the fuel.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The hostage is allowed to key the set at noon.

follow_up_signals.text: The vacancy sign at the Verity Motel went dark last night. Someone cut the power from the inside.
Room fourteen is empty. The hostage reached the shelter under a borrowed name and asked to keep it.

radio_broadcasts.source_name: Almshouse East Wing — Fever Ward Plea

message_fragments.text: ...east wing... I have sealed the ward... do not come in breathing hard... listen first...
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The ward is sealed from the inside — her doing, not the fever's.

message_fragments.text: Warden Otilia, St Brigid's east ward. Seven of us and one fever I can name from the old books. I have barred the door from my side to keep it in, not to keep help out. There is a course of antibiotics in the dispensary and nobody left who can walk to it.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The warden sealed the ward herself — protocol, not panic.

message_fragments.text: If you come: boiled water, gloved hands, and no promises about what you find. I will leave the dispensary ledger open on the table so you can see I am not hiding anything. I would rather be treated than mourned correctly.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: She names the fever from the old books.

message_fragments.text: The fever is in the third bed now. My voice is not what it was on the first day. Come before the ledger runs out of names.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The fever reached the third bed.

follow_up_signals.text: Warden Otilia reports the dispensary is packed, boiled, and waiting. She counts gloves as ammunition.
The east ward held. Otilia's ledger shows no new fever names for six days running.

message_fragments.text: Warehouse district, rack row nine. We cut the wrong column and the mezzanine came down on crew two. Three of us can still reach the radio.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: An accident reported like a work order.

message_fragments.text: We are not asking you to dig with your hands. There are jacks and slings in our own kit if you can stand at the other end of them. We kept the tools dry. Keep the channel open.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: They have their own jacks — they need hands, not tools.

follow_up_signals.text: Crew two is out from under the mezzanine. The row is shored with their own jacks and somebody's belt.
The salvage crew sends three pairs of working hands to the shelter as thanks. They would not stay for thanks.

message_fragments.text: This is not a rescue band. This is a bill. We hold a nomad courier who paddled into the wrong district. Her people know the toll.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The band announces a debt before a name.

message_fragments.text: The courier's name is Ilga and she has stopped bargaining for herself. She keeps asking whether her rope and boat made it to shore first. Tolls are due on the fourth day.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The courier stopped bargaining for herself.

message_fragments.text: Collect at Dentists' Row. The debt does not care who pays it. Nor do we, much.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: She asks after her rope and boat — not the ransom.

follow_up_signals.text: The nomads received word their courier is alive. The debt talks now, instead of counting.
Ilga is free. The river nomads remember who paid the debt, and the memory travels faster than the river.

message_fragments.text: ATTENTION SURVIVORS. Sector shelter is open. Proceed to the collapsed structure east of the tram depot. Bring your provisions. This is a civil-defense directive.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: A directive with no call sign and no return address.

message_fragments.text: The shelter has beds for two hundred. The shelter has heat. The shelter is not asking you to bring anything except everything you are carrying. Repeat: bring everything you are carrying.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The directive promises everything and asks nothing.

message_fragments.text: Civil defense stopped transmitting in the second winter. Whoever is reading this directive has the cadence right and the years wrong.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: Civil defense stopped transmitting in the second winter — this is not them.

follow_up_signals.text: The collapsed structure east of the tram depot held no beds and no heat. It held an ambush, and now it holds warnings.

message_fragments.text: Command Post Echo, automated. Twelve hourly. This beacon is not a monument.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The beacon insists it is not a monument.

message_fragments.text: Disregard the automated log. This is Sergeant Brenner, still commissioned by nobody, still counting. Four of us walked into the shoulder; two of us can still walk out of it. The ordnance is stable. The legs are not.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The automated log is overridden by a living voice.

message_fragments.text: We held the shoulder so the shells could not roll back downhill. Somebody should profit from that, and it will not be us.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: He counts the hours himself — nobody commissioned him.

message_fragments.text: If the beacon runs twelve more hours it runs without me. Bring a litter or bring nothing.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: Bring a litter or bring nothing.

follow_up_signals.text: Echo's beacon runs without the sergeant now. He is on the move, and he left the counting to the machine.
Brenner signed off at last: the shoulder still holds, the shells stay uphill, and the beacon finally sleeps.

message_fragments.text: Courier desk, salt route. The crossing took me and the ice took the road. I am short and honest about both.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: She reports her own shortage before asking for anything.

message_fragments.text: I holed up in the Shallows market stalls. Water is fine — it is the cold that is keeping the ledger. Weather looks to hold for perhaps four days. After that the ice road closes and so do I.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The courier is short and honest about both shortages.

message_fragments.text: If you come, come in weather you would cross in yourself. I would rather wait two days for someone who arrives than one day for someone the wind takes.
message_fragments.outcome_hint: The cold keeps the ledger — the water is fine.

follow_up_signals.text: Fresh footprints in the Shallows market stalls. Someone is keeping the ledger warm.
The courier crossed back with the salt route ledger intact. The crossing owes you a favour now, and couriers pay their favours.
